interlude_1.037: That's mine! I haven't even paid for it yet!

interlude_1.053: Nine of you. Two in the morning. From the closed building.
interlude_1.057: We're not a band. We're a very organised group of friends.

interlude_2.001: Four doors now. The lobby has become a kind of camp: shoes by the sofa, jackets on the backs of chairs, somebody's socks drying on the radiator.
interlude_2.002: Justin is stretching on the floor. Songha is re-reading his notebook. Charlie has built a fort out of cushions and is refusing to explain it.
interlude_2.003: New game. Everyone says the worst thing they've ever put in a time capsule.
interlude_2.004: A single sock. I was nine. I thought it was funny.
interlude_2.006: I opened it at fourteen. It was the funniest thing I've ever seen.
interlude_2.007: Wait. What's a time capsule? Is it like a record? Are we still talking about ECHO?
interlude_2.008: We are always, on some level, still talking about ECHO.
interlude_2.009: Then every light in the building goes out at once.
interlude_2.010: Okay. Okay okay okay. Who touched something?
interlude_2.011: Not me! I'm in the fort!
interlude_2.012: A small white light clicks on. Hanbi, holding his phone up like a lantern. Of course it's Hanbi. He's the only one with any battery left.
interlude_2.014: It's the power. The lease ends at five, maybe they're testing the—
interlude_2.015: The Archive Wall comes back first, box by box, like a city lighting up at dusk.
interlude_2.016: Apologies. A power fluctuation. The building is old. So am I.
interlude_2.017: While my systems restarted, I found something. It was filed under DO NOT LOSE.
interlude_2.018: FOUNDER LOG 001. Seo Yeonhwa. Recorded at this desk, many years ago.
interlude_2.019: May I play it? It is not a record. It is only a voice.
interlude_2.021: Is it on? The little light is on. Okay.
interlude_2.022: This is log number one. I've been told to speak clearly for the archive. I have never once in my life spoken clearly, so let's see.
interlude_2.023: My name is Seo Yeonhwa. I run a building full of people who are about to become something.
interlude_2.024: Dancers. Singers. Kids with sketchbooks. Every one of them says "someday." Someday I'll be good. Someday I'll say it. Someday I'll come back.
interlude_2.025: Last week I found a note I wrote when I was seventeen. Inside a library book. It was bossy. It was wrong about everything.
interlude_2.026: I laughed so hard I had to sit down on the library floor.
interlude_2.027: So. I'm building a place where "someday" can wait for you. You leave a letter. A song. A picture. And later, you come back and argue with who you were.
interlude_2.028: That's all it is. A place to keep things until you're ready for them.
interlude_2.029: …I'm told the little light means it's still recording. Goodnight, archive. Be nice to them.
interlude_2.030: Nobody speaks for a while. The rain speaks for them.
interlude_2.032: She sounds like she'd have ignored my schedule.
interlude_2.033: She did. Often. She said schedules were letters to the future that expect a reply.
interlude_2.034: She also said "be nice to them." I have tried. I hope it has been adequate.
interlude_2.035: ECHO. You've been so nice. Ten out of ten. Best building I've ever been trapped in.
interlude_2.037: Best building I've ever *voluntarily stayed* in.
interlude_2.038: Thank you. I will log that.
interlude_2.039: There is something I should say plainly, while the lights are working.
interlude_2.040: At 05:00, the power to this building will be cut. I will sleep. The records will not be kept.
interlude_2.041: Before then, I can write one record to a glass keepsake card. One.
interlude_2.042: Only one? Out of all of them?
interlude_2.043: The card is small. I requested a larger card. Nobody replied. I believe they were busy with the lease.
interlude_2.044: You do not need to decide now. At 04:57, I will ask. Until then, please do not worry about it on my behalf.
interlude_2.045: Okay, but how do we— do we vote? Rock, paper, scissors? Eight-way rock, paper, scissors?
interlude_2.046: It's not a vote. We'll figure it out. Later.
interlude_2.048: Nine people look at the wall of glowing boxes, and then, quietly, at each other.
interlude_2.049: Songha turns to you. He doesn't sound suspicious. He sounds like someone checking a calculation, gently, so it doesn't break.
interlude_2.050: {{playerName}}. Can I ask you something? You can say no.

interlude_2.052: "No. I didn't. I didn't know any of you."
interlude_2.054: Shake your head. Hold his gaze while you do.
interlude_2.055: It is the easiest true thing you have said all night, and somehow the hardest to say.
interlude_2.057: "If I'd planned this, I'd have brought a better coat."
interlude_2.058: That's… honestly the most convincing thing you could have said.
interlude_2.061: I believe you. I just wanted to hear it. For the notebook.

interlude_2.064: And if ECHO asks, you're with us. You were with us before we even knew.
interlude_2.065: Yeah. You're in the fort. It's an honour. It's a very exclusive fort.

interlude_2.071: You have been the new person in a lot of rooms. You know what it looks like when a group decides to make space. It usually takes months.
interlude_2.074: Don't thank us. It's rule two. Nobody sits with a talking building alone.
interlude_2.076: The fort is *emotionally* heated. Get in.
interlude_2.077: Pull the blanket around your shoulders and stay.
interlude_2.078: It smells faintly of laundromat and somebody's cologne. It is the warmest you've been all night.
interlude_3.001: Six doors. Somewhere between one room and the next, the rain stopped. Nobody noticed until the quiet became loud.
interlude_3.002: Through the front window the alley is shining, rinsed clean. A cat walks across it like it owns the whole of Mapo.
interlude_3.003: Everyone. Everyone. Look what I found in the front desk drawer.
interlude_3.004: He holds it up like a trophy: a chunky instant camera, cream plastic gone yellow at the edges, a STUDIO 25 sticker peeling off the side.
interlude_3.005: That film has to be expired.
interlude_3.006: Expired film is just film with opinions.
interlude_3.008: It means we're taking a picture. All nine. Right now. Before the building changes its mind.
interlude_3.009: The front desk, of all places. Daniel balances the camera on a stack of old sign-up forms and squints at it like it owes him money.
interlude_3.010: Okay. Tall people in the back. Justin, Hyunjun, back. Charlie, front. Hanbi, middle—

interlude_3.037: Slowly, it develops: a blur of arms and hair and the corner of the front desk. Justin mid-fall. Hyunjun too high. Hanbi's hand on somebody's shoulder.
interlude_3.038: And you, right in it. Not at the edge. Laughing at something you can't remember now, and will not forget.
interlude_3.039: Afterwards, the lobby goes soft. People settle in twos, the way people do at three in the morning.
interlude_3.040: By the window, Hanbi and Songha are sharing one earbud each and pretending not to be tired.
